11-136.r: Order of launch: TRYSEM (August 1979; rural youth aged 18-35) → RLEGP (15 August 1983) → JRY (April 1989) → EAS (latest).

11-137.r: TRYSEM (Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment, August 1979) → rural development; a component of IRDP; merged into SGSY in April 1999.

11-138.r: MRTP (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices) Act, 1969 → controls monopolies, not an anti-poverty programme; RLEGP, IRDP, NREP → anti-poverty programmes.

11-139.r: Rural Infrastructure Development Fund → created in and administered by NABARD (1995-96, corpus Rs. 2,000 crore); 39 eligible activities; rural industries are not a RIDF programme.

11-142.r: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana → 1 April 1989, Seventh Plan (1985-90), by merging NREP and RLEGP; replaced by Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana on 1 April 1999.

11-143.r: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1 April 1989, PM Rajiv Gandhi) → extra wage employment in rural areas; Centre:State cost 80:20; 30% of jobs reserved for women.
11-143.t: Launched under Rajiv Gandhi, not Indira Gandhi; meant for the rural, not urban, poor.

11-146.r: Wrong pair: JRY – April 1995; JRY began 1 April 1989 (NREP + RLEGP). Correct: TRYSEM – August 1979; NREP – October 1980; SGSY – April 1999.

11-147.r: IRDP → begun 1978-79, nationwide from 2 October 1980; aim: lift rural BPL households above the poverty line through income-generating assets/self-employment.

11-149.r: SGSY (April 1999) restructured IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, Million Wells Scheme, SITRA and Ganga Kalyan Yojana; JRY was not included.

11-150.r: SGSY (1 April 1999) → merged six programmes (IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, GKY, MWS); group approach; skill upgradation; lift BPL families above poverty line. All four correct.

11-152.r: National Rural Livelihood Mission (June 2011) → restructured SGSY; fully replaced it from 1 April 2013; renamed DAY-NRLM on 29 March 2016.

11-153.r: NRLM (DAY-NRLM) → better rural livelihoods by strengthening SHGs and skill development; aims to cover 7 crore poor households; no new industries or free farm inputs.

11-154.r: Wrong pairs: SJSRY (1 December 1997) → urban, not rural, employment; social security is not part of Bharat Nirman. Correct: SIDBI – industrial finance; NABARD – rural credit.
11-154.c: Answer not printed; two pairs (b and d) are wrong, so the single-answer question has no unique key.

11-155.r: Nehru Rojgar Yojana (October 1989, end of Seventh Plan) → urban poor; three schemes: Urban Micro Enterprises, Urban Wage Employment, Housing and Shelter Upgradation.

11-156.r: SJSRY (1 December 1997) → subsumed Nehru Rozgar Yojana, Urban Basic Services for the Poor and PM's Integrated Urban Poverty Eradication Programme; not PM's Rozgar Yojana.

11-157.r: Krishi Shramik Samajik Suraksha Yojana → 2001; SGSY → 1999; Employment Assurance Scheme → 1993; PM Gramodaya Yojana → 2000.

11-158.r: SGSY → 1999; Swarnajayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana → 1997; Jawahar Rozgar Yojana → 1989; National Rural Health Mission → 2005.

11-159.r: National Rural Health Mission → 2005; National Social Assistance Programme → 1995; SGSY → 1999; Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana → 2001.

11-160.r: Wrong pair: MGNREGA – 2003. NREGA 2005 in force 2 February 2006, renamed MGNREGA 2 October 2009. Correct: Janshree Bima – 2000; NRHM – 2005; Aam Aadmi Bima – 2007.

11-161.r: RMSA (Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, March 2009) → secondary education, not employment; MGNREGA, NRLM, STEP (for women, 1986-87) → employment programmes.

11-162.r: NREGA → passed 23 August 2005; in force 2 February 2006 in 200 districts (330 in 2007-08); all-India from 1 April 2008; renamed MGNREGA 2 October 2009.

11-167.r: MGNREGA → livelihood security: at least 100 days of wage work a year per rural household (unskilled manual work); builds durable assets; a legal right, not just a scheme.

11-170.r: Incorrect about NREGA: 'transparency and accountability not possible' – the Act has many built-in transparency and accountability measures. It lists permitted works and guarantees employment.

11-171.r: MGNREGA allocation, Budget 2009-10 → Rs. 39,100 crore (option Rs. 39,000 crore), 149% more than Rs. 16,000 crore in 2008-09.

11-172.r: Budget 2020-21 vs 2019-20 → only PMJAY-Ayushman Bharat allocation fell (from Rs. 6556 crore); MGNREGA rose (60000 → 61500 crore); Mid-day Meal unchanged; Ganga plan rose.

11-173.r: Budget 2023-24 → steepest % cut: Atma Nirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (not MGNREGA); highest % growth: Reform Linked Distribution Scheme (not Jal Jeevan Mission). Neither statement correct.

11-174.r: MGNREGA → guarantees 100 days of wage employment a year to each rural household (not to every adult member) whose adults do unskilled manual work.
11-174.t: The 100 days are per household, not per adult member.

11-175.r: MGNREGA results → higher rural wages and purchasing power, less distress migration to cities, more (not less) bargaining power for labourers.

11-176.r: Indira Gandhi Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme (Rajasthan, 2022) → 100 days (125 days from 2023) of work a year per urban family; work within 15 days of registration, not 30.

11-177.r: Passage on giving workers 'a sense of partnership and cooperative performance' → Community Development; India's Community Development Programme began 1952 with Ford Foundation help.

11-178.r: Community Development Programme (2 October 1952) → multi-purpose overall rural development: agriculture, animal husbandry, irrigation, education, health, living conditions; so more than one option fits.

11-180.r: Chronology: Key Village Scheme → Community Development Programme (October 1952) → Democratic Decentralization (Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, 1957) → DRDA at district level.

11-183.r: Community Development Programme (2 October 1952) → set the stage for organization of Panchayati Raj.

11-184.r: Architect of community development in India → S.K. Dey, first Cooperative and Panchayati Raj Minister; Community Development Programme began 1952 under PM Nehru.

11-185.r: National Extension Service → 1953; begun because the Community Development Programme (1952) could not cover all India for lack of funds; wider coverage at less cost.

11-186.r: Among the options, National Extension Service (1953) → the first programme of community development; Cooperation Movement and IRDP are not.

11-187.r: Antyodaya Programme → first started by Rajasthan (1977-78); 'Antyodaya' = rise (Udaya) of the poorest of the poor.

11-188.r: All true then: Antyodaya → wheat Rs. 2/kg, rice Rs. 3/kg; Old Age Pension → Rs. 75/month Central share; BPL family → 25 kg grain monthly below half cost.

11-189.r: Atal Pension Yojana (9 May 2015) → minimum guaranteed pension (Rs. 1000-5000/month) mainly for unorganized workers; same pension to spouse after subscriber's death.
11-189.t: Statement 'only one family member can join' is wrong.

11-190.r: NPS (regulated by PFRDA) → citizens (resident or non-resident) and OCIs aged 18-70; Central staff (not Armed Forces) joining from 1 January 2004; State staff after State notification.
11-190.t: Armed Forces are excluded, and the Central date is 1 January 2004, not 1 April 2004.

11-192.r: PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-dhan (NPS-Traders, 2019) → traders/self-employed aged 18-40, turnover up to Rs. 1.5 crore; voluntary, contributory; minimum pension Rs. 3000/month. NPS members not eligible.

11-193.r: PM Kisan Maan-dhan Yojana → launched 12 September 2019 at Ranchi; small and marginal farmers get Rs. 3000/month pension after age 60; spouse gets 50% on death.

11-194.r: PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (2019) → voluntary, contributory pension for unorganized sector workers; minimum assured pension Rs. 3000 per month after age 60.

11-195.r: Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001) → insurance for workers who lose jobs; up to 30% of annual salary paid till new work is found or for one year, whichever is earlier.

11-196.r: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2 October 2007) → social security for rural landless BPL labourers; head or an earning member aged 18-59 insured; run with States/UTs and LIC.

11-197.r: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2 October 2007) → insures head or earning member of a rural landless household; scholarship for up to two children from class 9. Wrong: age 30-65.

11-199.r: ESI Scheme (ESI Act, 1948) → social insurance for sickness, maternity, disablement, employment-injury death; covers employees of hotels, motor transport, newspapers, private medical institutions (all four).

11-200.r: Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act → passed by Parliament in 2008; notified 30 December 2008.

11-201.r: SJSRY → employment generation, not social security; Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana, National Health Insurance Scheme, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act 2008 → social security.

11-202.r: Skill Development Programme → vocational training, not social protection; RSBY, Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act 2008 → social protection measures.

11-203.r: PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (Budget 2015-16) → personal accident cover, ages 18-70 (not 18-50); premium Rs. 12 a year; announced with PMJJBY and Atal Pension Yojana.

11-204.r: National Social Security Fund (2011, Rs. 1000 crore) → social security for unorganized workers, not an employment/poverty programme; MGNREGA, NRLM, SJSRY are.

11-205.r: All matched: HRIDAY → Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana; SEHAT → Social Endeavour for Health and Telemedicine; AMRUT → Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation.
11-205.c: Option (b) says 'Healthcare' though the correct name has 'Health'; the book still treats it as matched.

11-206.r: Wrong pair: Swachh Bharat Mission – safe drinking water; SBM (2 October 2014) is for sanitation. Correct: UDAY – discom finances; HRIDAY – heritage cities; AMRUT – urban infrastructure.

11-207.r: Swachh Bharat Mission → began 2 October 2014; target Open Defecation Free 'Clean India' by 2 October 2019 (Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary); Rural and Urban parts.
hi: Open Defecation Free (खुले में शौच मुक्त)

11-209.r: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II → from 1 April 2020, period 2020-21 to 2024-25; outlay Rs. 1,40,881 crore; ODF Plus, solid and liquid waste management.

11-210.r: 10-Year Rural Sanitation Strategy (2019-2029) → launched 27 September 2019 by DDWS, Ministry of Jal Shakti, to sustain SBM-G behaviour change.

11-211.r: Swachh Bharat Mission (2014) → focuses on collective behaviour change of the whole community, since rural open defecation is tied to morning walks, crop checks, socializing. Both correct.

11-212.r: 'Swachhata Hi Seva' → countrywide awareness campaign launched by PM Modi on 15 September 2018; held from 15 September to 2 October.

11-213.r: Swachh Survekshan 2022 → Indore first 7-star garbage-free city; Surat, Bhopal, Navi Mumbai, Mysuru, Vishakhapatnam, Tirupati got 5-star; so none of the options is excluded.

11-214.r: Swachh Survekshan 2021 (1 lakh+ population) → Indore first, Surat second, Vijayawada third; Tirupati not in top three. 2023 → Indore and Surat joint first, Navi Mumbai third.

11-215.r: Swachh Survekshan 2021 → Uttar Pradesh sixth among States with 100+ Urban Local Bodies; in 2023 U.P. ranked 9th and Maharashtra was the cleanest State.

11-216.r: Rural cleanliness survey → Sikkim was top at question time; Swachh Survekshan Grameen 2022 → Telangana 1st, Haryana 2nd, Tamil Nadu 3rd among larger States.
11-216.c: Printed answer is (d) Telangana, but the explanation says option (b) Sikkim was correct for the question period; Telangana tops only the 2022 survey.

11-217.r: Rural people do not see open defecation as a threat (A true); purity-pollution norms kept toilets out of homes (R true); R does not explain A.

11-218.r: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan → sanitation programme revamping Total Sanitation Campaign to make India Open Defecation Free (WASH approach); so 'none of the above'.

11-219.r: Nirmal Gram Puraskar (October 2003; first awards 2005) → incentive award for fully sanitized, open defecation free Panchayats, Blocks, Districts, States under Total Sanitation Campaign.

11-220.r: Rashtriya Garima Abhiyaan → eradicate manual scavenging and rehabilitate manual scavengers (per the 2013 Act prohibiting manual scavenging).

11-221.r: Toilet revolution → Government subsidy and loans for building flush toilets in villages and cities, to prevent infectious diseases.

11-222.r: Integrated Low Cost Sanitation (1980-81) → end dry latrines and free manual scavengers; funded on sharing basis with 75% Central subsidy; State subsidy is not 25%.

11-223.r: National Social Assistance Programme (15 August 1995, Article 41) → includes National Family Benefit Scheme, Annapurna, old age pension; not Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana.

11-225.r: IGNOAPS (19 November 2007) → BPL persons aged 60+ (lowered from 65 on 1 April 2011); Central pension initially Rs. 200/month, not Rs. 300.

11-226.r: Minimum Needs Programme (Fifth Plan, 1974-78) → basic services for rural and urban population; 'investment in human' approach; social forestry not included.

11-229.r: Liberalization of economy → economic reform, not a measure to reduce inequality; Minimum Needs Programme, taxation, land reforms → reduce inequality.

11-230.r: SVAMITVA → Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of Panchayati Raj (not Mines); drone mapping of rural Abadi land; 'Record of Rights' to owners. Incorrect: statements 1 and 3.

11-231.r: PM Awas Yojana → launched June 2015 for 'Housing for All' by 2022 (span 2015-2022 at question time); Urban and Gramin parts.
11-231.c: Answer not printed; the explanation says option (c) 2015-2022 was correct then.

11-233.r: Indira Awas Yojana (1985, part of RLEGP) → houses for rural BPL SCs/STs and freed bonded labourers at cheaper cost; in JRY from 1989; independent from 1 January 1996.

11-234.r: Rajiv Awas Yojana (June 2011) → 'Slum free India'; preparatory phase till June 2013; extended till 2022.

11-237.r: Kendriya Vidyalayas → scheme approved November 1962 (Second Central Pay Commission); formally set up 15 December 1963 as 'Central Schools'.

11-238.r: Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (2004) → schooling for girls, mainly SC, ST, OBC, minority, in educationally backward blocks with low female rural literacy.

11-239.r: 'Education for All' (Millennium Development Goal 2) → every child to complete primary schooling by 2015; SDG target 4.1 carries it forward.
11-239.c: Answer not printed; the explanation says option (b) 2015 was correct then.

11-240.r: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (2001) → universal elementary education for children aged 6-14 by 2010, with State Governments and local bodies.

11-243.r: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan allocation, Union Budget 2006-07 → Rs. 10,041 crore; National Education Mission 2023-24 → Rs. 38953 crore (budget estimate).

11-244.r: Saakshar Bharat (September 2009, restructured National Literacy Mission) → main focus on female literacy; cut adult non-literacy.

11-245.r: Right to Education Act, 2009 (in force from April 2010) → free and compulsory elementary education for children aged 6-14.

11-246.r: Right to free and compulsory education → Centre bears 68% of the expenditure; every child aged 6 to 14 has the right.

11-247.r: Look East Policy → foreign policy, not social development; Mid-day Meal (15 August 1995, NP-NSPE; PM POSHAN from 2021), Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rural Health Mission → social development.
